parsed.explanation: Strong national protections and no documented trans-specific border, facility, custody or care restriction for visitors. The main exposure is societal: equality bodies report rising anti-LGBTQI violence and intimidation, with trans people especially affected, an app-based ambush pattern, high harassment prevalence in the capital region, and a hate-crime recording gap despite legal prohibition. The subnational gender-registration conflict is resident-facing and unreconciled; it does not document a visitor-facing barrier. No trans-specific homicide count permits severity inference. The result is Reduced Risk: formal acceptance and functioning recourse, offset by documented social hostility and uneven hate-crime handling.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific border or document mismatch incident documented.
entry_documents.protection: Self-determination and anti-discrimination framework suggest institutional competence; travel guide describes welcoming destination.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor uses home passport; no documented referral or refusal pathway tied to trans status.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented police detention, custody placement, or investigation targeting trans visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No criminalisation of trans identity or expression documented; general legal protections exist.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Hate-crime prosecution is hampered by lack of statutory definition and recording code, but no custody exposure is documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented bathroom, ward, shelter, or facility exclusion aimed at trans visitors.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Anti-discrimination law covers gender identity in services; no facility restriction documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Resident gender-registration conflict in one region is not shown to govern visitor facilities.

care_services.exposure: No documented denial of emergency or routine care to trans visitors.
care_services.protection: Conversion practices banned; anti-discrimination framework covers services; no trans-specific care ban documented.
care_services.interaction: LGR process conflict is resident-facing and does not document visitor care denial.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Equality bodies report rising violence and intimidation against LGBTQI people, trans people especially affected; hate crimes lack statutory definition and recording code.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate motive has been recognised in court and non-discrimination law prohibits GI hate speech; institutional hostility largely absent.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police record app-trap incidents but many go unreported; prosecution proceeds under general provisions.

minors_guardians.exposure: No documented visitor-facing risk specific to a trans minor travelling with a guardian.
minors_guardians.protection: National LGR for resident minors is narrow, but no border, facility or care restriction on visiting minors is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parental-consent and psychological-opinion rules are resident LGR rules, not visitor entry rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented anti-LGBTQI violence and intimidation; dating-app ambush pattern involving robbery, humiliation and assault; 90% of LGBT respondents in capital region reported verbal or psychological harassment in 2019.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate motive recognised in court; first hate-motivated murder conviction in 2014; police have recorded app-trap incidents.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists but is weakened by missing hate-crime definition, underreporting and fear/shame.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Hate-crime recording gap and unresolved subnational gender-registration document conflict create uncertainty.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have recognised hate motive; equality bodies and anti-discrimination law provide formal recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: The subnational conflict concerns resident registration, not visitor documents; its effect on local offices is unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar formal equality, policing and review structures, and similar residual street-violence uncertainty. This dossier has stronger national self-ID and anti-discrimination law but weaker hate-crime recording and higher documented anti-LGBTQI harassment, so it sits slightly below that anchor.

The 0.85-B anchor documents specialist border training, legal aid, body cameras and functioning tribunal remedies. This dossier has no documented trans-specific border friction, but its unresolved hate-crime framework and rising violence record leave less verified traveler-facing assurance.

The 0.55-B anchor centres on discretionary border screening, refused admission and document mismatch. This dossier documents no such trans-specific border exposure, so it is materially safer than that anchor despite real social-violence concerns.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is formally protective: national self-determination, anti-discrimination covering gender identity, hate-speech prohibition, marriage/adoption equality and a conversion-practice ban. No dossier item documents a trans visitor being refused entry, placed in birth-sex custody, barred from facilities or denied care. The operative weakness is social and prosecutorial: rising anti-LGBTQI violence, trans people especially affected, app-based ambushes, high harassment prevalence and a hate-crime definition gap. The capital-region registration conflict is resident-facing and unresolved, not a visitor rule. Weighing documented acceptance and formal recourse against documented societal hostility and uneven hate-crime handling yields Reduced Risk rather than Low Risk.
